issue.description:
ADR-005's shipped ready_frontier check warns on every open issue carrying an assignee and explicitly documents the drawback that there is no way to mark an assignment as intentionally held, so an operator who deliberately parks work under a named assignee gets a permanent warning and learns to ignore the check. Add an advisory annotation on the assignment (distinct from manual_blocked, which gates the bead itself rather than the assignment) that the ready_frontier diagnostic treats as an acknowledged hold; keep doctor diagnose-don't-mutate (it must never clear or set the annotation), cover it with doctor tests and checkpoint round-trip, and document the field in the schema field guide.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Add a way to mark an assignment as an intentional hold so the doctor warning can exclude it

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: /home/coding/bead-rs/docs/plan/plan.md (section 6.2.1, R026, section 13 activation gate)
Authorized by: docs/adr/003-automatic-checkpoint-flush-gated-on-incremental-publication.md

## Overview
Make a successful semantic mutation publish a checkpoint generation covering its own committed sequence, replacing explicit sync flush-only as the default, so the durable checkpoint is never silently behind the database.

Gated. Per-mutation publication against the current path would write bytes quadratic in mutation count into a Git-tracked directory: flush is linear in workspace size, each generation leaks a full-workspace-sized object that is never collected, and most mutation kinds never advance the sequence that signals a flush is needed. The prerequisites are the implementation converging on plan sections 6.1.1 and 6.2 as already written; each is worth fixing whether or not the default ever changes.

bead-rs still never invokes Git. Automatic Git publication remains rejected.

## Progress
- [ ] P1: content-addressed monolithic root
- [ ] P2: applied pointer-declared tombstones
- [ ] P3: audit event for every committed semantic mutation (create, dep, ref, data, enumeration test)
- [ ] P4: reachable sharded publication
- [ ] A1-A6: chokepoint, skip-when-clean, publication lock, split-failure semantics, escape hatches, capability handshake
- [ ] A7: documentation reversal
- [ ] A8: activation gate evidence, then flip the default

All checklist items confirmed: P1 content-addressed root, P2 applied tombstones, P3 per-mutation audit events, P4 sharded publication, A1-A6, A7 wording reversal, A8 evidence + flip. AUTO_FLUSH_COMPILED_DEFAULT=true retained in src/service/checkpoint.rs:230. Sole blocks edge (beadrs-f42b12c7 activation evidence) closed; all R026 child beads closed. Re-ran the full section-13 gate on this tree: the 9 evidence suites (54 tests) plus f017 identical-content reuse (55th) all pass, and an e2e probe confirmed a plain 'bead create' publishes its own covering generation with 'sync flush-only' reporting 'Checkpoint already current' exit 0, while --no-auto-flush suppresses publication. No source changes needed; nothing to commit. Side finding: a stale copy of this repo's beads.db had been leaked at /run/user/1000/.beads by an earlier test run (strict subset of the live store, verified 0 unique IDs) and was breaking local gate runs via R030 discovery — removed it as machine-local ephemera.

issue.description:
ADR-005 (Accepted 2026-08-16) documents that open-but-assigned issues are silently excluded from the ready frontier with no diagnostic — the state that stranded 583 issues across 47 workspaces and fully starved ten of them while doctor reported healthy. No open bead implements the accepted decision. Add a `ready_frontier` check to `bead doctor` under the `dependencies` scope that warns when open issues carry an assignee, names a bounded sample of the offending ids, and states the exact remedy (`bead update <id> --clear-assignee`). Strictly advisory: doctor never clears an assignee, not even under `--repair`.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Add doctor ready_frontier check for assigned open issues (ADR-005)
